q: A full-time nanny would cost […] 60–70% of my take-home pay
cx: First-time pregnant consultant on six figures weighing staying home versus a nanny.

q: I’ve been having lots of convos with ChatGPT and something that stuck that it asked me was this:
cx: She has been using ChatGPT to think through whether to stay home after the birth.

q: Mat leave is 4 months but with PTO I could extend it to 5 months.
cx: Her leave length, stretched with paid time off, before a nanny would be needed.

q: I love hearing positive SAHM stories 🫶. I know it’s not all rainbows and butterflies but it’s nice to hear after seeing a lot of negative content online about it.
cx: Reacting to replies from stay-at-home mothers after negative content online.

q: HR at my work hasn't been very communicative since I informed them of the pregnancy and started planning my leave. An example, after I sent in my leave plan they never responded confirming they recieved it or what the next steps are, I didn't even know it was approved until they sent out the temporary job listing for my position a month later.
cx: Two weeks before her leave starts, HR still has not explained how to enter it.

q: they're implementing a whole new leave system starting 9/1/26 and anyone who has leave on the old system from then on and after will have to resubmit it on the new system. They'll also have a training via zoom for us on August 12, the very first day of my maternity leave.
cx: A company-wide email changes the leave system mid-leave; training falls on her first day off.

q: starting 1/1/27 we go from 6 weeks to 14 weeks of paid parental leave for my company, I return 1/4/27, is there any way I can ask if that can be applied to my leave now instead of missing out on it?
cx: Paid parental leave rises from 6 to 14 weeks three days before she returns.

q: while he comes to every appointment, he otherwise seems checked out or uninterested. Physical affection and emotional reassurance have dropped off, the nursery has only a layer of primer on the wall with nothing else done, I have purchased all of the baby stuff besides for half of the stroller, and I have paid for all of my medical bills.
cx: First pregnancy, due in autumn; she feels unsupported by her husband and friends.

q: I'd rather lean on my own family emotionally and in the event of any in-home support post birth. I'm hesitant to rely too much on my in-laws because I'm worried they'll smother me/us in how they want to provide support. They instead take this as a slight
cx: Planning who helps after the birth; in-laws nearby take her preference as a slight.

q: it's the weirdest elephant in the room to not discuss any part of my pregnancy when they are asking if I am preordering a game that comes out when I am on maternity leave
cx: First in her friend group to have a baby; friends talk games instead.

q: I’ve been trying to find classes but they are all full for pregnancy/prenatal, I should have started my search sooner it seems.
cx: Looking for prenatal yoga late in pregnancy.

q: Small community, I can’t even get a hospital tour before due date unless someone cancels their slot😩
cx: Small town; hospital tours are booked up until after her due date.

q: She questioned if I understood how much pain I would be in and how I plan on looking after my other children.
cx: UK mother of three asking a consultant for a planned caesarean at 33 weeks.
r: procedure decision (requested caesarean), previous loss and medical history in unit

q: she did give me the consent form but she acted like I was an inconvenience for it.
cx: The consultant agreed to book the caesarean but made her feel a nuisance.

q: no matter what concern was brought up, she just kept telling me not to eat anything except protein to stop the baby from growing and said it should be easy to cut everything else out of my diet since I only have 3 weeks left. From her own personal experience, she didn’t want a big baby so she only ate tofu and kale the entire time
cx: At 38 weeks with a large baby, her midwife answers every concern with a diet rule.
r: medical (fetal size, diet as treatment), induction decision

q: I really want to not worry, that’s why I wish my providers would just have a real conversation with me about concerns/reasons to not be concerned.
cx: Second baby; distrust of her midwives drives most of her worry, she says.

q: Like every sound they make, every mess, just exhausts me to NO END.
cx: 27 weeks pregnant with her fourth, three boys aged 5, 2.5 and 17 months at home.

q: Second kid, first time breastfeeding.
cx: Eleven days after her second birth; feeding did not work out the first time.

q: A lactation consultant is not in the cards right now. I am having a a lot of difficulty finding one that works with my insurance, and I cannot afford to pay the rates out of pocket. I live in a HCOL area so they are all $250-$300 plus just for a consult visit.
cx: Newborn sleepy at the breast; no in-network lactation consultant.

q: what are some signs, traits, &c. you see as being general predictive factors that someone will likely have a generally good pregnancy and/or labor experience?
cx: Asks birth professionals what predicts an easier pregnancy or labour.

q: He is my first and probably my only child; it's important to me to have him naturally. If I can't, that's okay; I just really want a natural birth.
cx: Same day as a diagnosis at 27 weeks; her sister needed a caesarean.

q: I’m currently crying my eyes out because the one thing I’ve been so scared about is the actual labor and delivery itself.  I’m so scared about feeling everything, the pain, any painful check up or tool they’ll use on me.
cx: Night before her induction at 40+5, first baby.

q: It really helps me calm my nerves a bit hearing other women’s stories.
cx: Replying to strangers' induction stories the night before hers.

q: Everyone keeps telling me it will get better, and frankly, it’s just gotten worst.  I keep telling everyone that I never want to do this again, and they said I will forget it all when I have a baby in my arms.
cx: 28 weeks, first pregnancy, sick since week 7.

q: I am so tired, and I barely have the energy to work let alone prepare our house (which is currently being remodeled, started pre-pregnancy).
cx: Working from home at 28 weeks while the house is half-remodelled.

q: He’s really been a trooper, but he’s definitely out of his depth.
cx: Her husband cleans up after her vomiting weekly.
